portInfo.description: Castries concentrates Saint Lucia’s cruise traffic. SLASPA describes Pointe Seraphine as the island’s dedicated cruise shopping/berth complex within walking distance of the city, with La Place Carenage serving ships at the Queen Elizabeth II docks and water taxis linking the two retail hubs; it also publishes Pointe Seraphine berth lengths/depths and multi-use berth dimensions. The commercial Saint Lucia Cruise Port site (GPH) markets a redeveloped arrivals terminal, lists Pointe Seraphine PS1/PS2 at 250 m / 245 m LOA with 9.0 m draught plus larger numbered berths, and reports 2024 call/passenger totals. Because the two official-facing tables do not match line-for-line, SeaDays records both citations and leaves reconciliation as an open question rather than picking a silent “winner.”

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Castries market — check opening hours locally on your call day.
Pointe Seraphine / La Place Carenage shopping
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask which berth number you are on — Castries can host multiple ships.
